_README: The DECLARED alignment contract for L6. It names the toolchain this repository intends to certify,
build and run on -- deliberately the INTENDED one, from the moment the verifier exists, rather than
the status quo. That makes L6 fail truthfully today: CI certifies on Node 24.14.0 while production
builds and runs on v22.22.1, a major-version gap sitting in the middle of the identity invariant.
P1.4b does NOT edit this file. P1.4b changes production until production matches it.
CROSS-PLATFORM HONESTY. L6 has two halves and they compare different things:
half A  certified <-> build: VERSIONS only. CI runs on windows-latest and production builds on
Linux x86-64, so Node 24.14.0 for Windows and Node 24.14.0 for Linux are different
executables with different digests, necessarily and forever. Comparing them would be a
check that can only ever fail.
half B  build <-> workers: the exact Linux executable -- path, version and SHA-256 read through
/proc/<pid>/exe, which is the running image even if the on-disk binary was replaced.
npm is not pinned by the workflow -- it ships with the Node distribution -- so ci_npm is recorded as
unpinned and is not compared. The declared npm is compared against the BUILD npm only.
